ideas.title: Snow Globe of Your Year
ideas.summary: A glass snow globe on a little wooden base. Shake it (drag, swipe or shake the phone) and tiny objects from their year swirl with the snow, then settle into a scene.
ideas.suitable_if: Always, as long as you know a few real things about them. With almost no context, make the scene their city or a season they love.

ideas.title: The Pop-Up Hello
ideas.summary: A closed card on the table. Open it and a paper diorama of their world unfolds in 3D, layer by layer, with your first letter as their Secret Santa tucked inside.

ideas.title: Your Holographic Trading Card
ideas.summary: A rare holographic trading card of them. Tilt it and the foil shimmers; flip it for absurdly precise stats, special moves and a rarity rating.
ideas.suitable_if: You know at least four real traits or habits.

ideas.title: A Tiny Companion
ideas.summary: A small animated character of their pet (or a creature inspired by them) lives on the page. It watches the cursor, reacts to clicks, falls asleep if ignored, and has one secret trick.
ideas.suitable_if: They have a pet, or you know enough about them to design a creature they'd recognise.

ideas.title: The Game of Your Year
ideas.summary: A well-designed little game where they (or their pet) travel through their year, level by level. The collectibles are this season's gifts; the final level ends on a real celebration.

ideas.title: The Premiere
ideas.summary: A cinema. The curtains open on an animated short film about their December and their year, with opening titles, a soundtrack, a blooper reel and end credits listing everyone in their life.
ideas.suitable_if: You know their people and some moments of their year.

ideas.title: The Tiny World
ideas.summary: An explorable little island or village. Every gift they opened this season lives somewhere in it — the snow globe on a shelf, the jelly fruits at the market, the fish in the harbour — and clicking each one brings back a memory.

ideas.title: Escape the Workshop
ideas.summary: They're locked in their Secret Santa's workshop on Christmas Eve. The puzzles use things only they know and the gifts from this season. The last lock opens to the final present.

ideas.title: The Pop-Up Diorama
ideas.summary: A large illustrated pop-up of one moment from their year — a summit, a launch day, a trip — with pull-tabs, wheels and flaps that move parts of the scene.
ideas.suitable_if: You know one meaningful moment well.

ideas.title: Something in the Envelope
ideas.summary: A 3D envelope with a wax seal. Break the seal; what comes out is unexpected — a letter that unfolds into a map, a pressed flower, a ticket to an imaginary place, a tiny origami animal.
ideas.suitable_if: Always. A strong tier S choice.

ideas.title: The Matchbox of Tiny Things
ideas.summary: A matchbox with a hand-drawn label. Slide the drawer to find five miniature objects, each with a tiny museum label explaining its absurd significance in their life.
ideas.suitable_if: You know at least five concrete things about them.

ideas.title: Scratch to Win
ideas.summary: A lottery scratch card. Scratch the silver to reveal absurdly specific "prizes" for their life — "One (1) meeting cancelled by someone else", "Dog walk with no rain".

ideas.title: Message in a Bottle
ideas.summary: A bottle bobbing on a gentle sea. Pull the cork, tip the bottle, and a rolled letter slides out and unrolls.
ideas.suitable_if: You know enough for the letter to be specific.

ideas.title: A Jelly Fruit
ideas.summary: A translucent jelly version of a fruit they love, on a little plate. Pull it and it stretches and springs back; tap it and it wobbles; a secret gesture cuts it.
ideas.suitable_if: You know a fruit or flavour they love, or a place known for one.

ideas.title: The Fish Tank
ideas.summary: A glass aquarium. Each fish is named after a person, pet or in-joke in their life and behaves accordingly. Tap the glass, drop food, find the hidden treasure chest.
ideas.suitable_if: You know some of their people, pets or jokes.

ideas.title: The Crystal of Good Things
ideas.summary: A slowly turning crystal. Each facet holds one good thing from their year; rotate it to catch the light on each one.

ideas.title: The Hot-Air Balloon
ideas.summary: A little balloon drifting over an illustrated map of the places in their year. Steer it; at each place a banner unrolls with a memory. Blow into the microphone (optional) to lift it.
ideas.suitable_if: You know places from their year.

ideas.title: Bubble Wrap of Small Worries
ideas.summary: A sheet of bubble wrap. Every pop releases a tiny absurd worry from their life and resolves it ("The tests passed. Even the flaky one.").

ideas.title: Their Personal Magic 8-Ball
ideas.summary: A magic 8-ball whose answers come from their world — in the voice of their pet, their favourite show, their mountain guide.
ideas.suitable_if: You know a voice they'd recognise.

ideas.title: A Bouquet That Blooms
ideas.summary: A bouquet of closed buds wrapped in paper. Each flower blooms when touched, and the card explains why each flower was chosen for them.

ideas.title: A Garden That Grows Today
ideas.summary: A small pot with seeds. Water them and they grow over real minutes during the day. Come back tonight and it's in full flower.

ideas.title: A Glass Ornament
ideas.summary: A hand-blown glass ornament with a tiny scene inside. Turn it to look inside; tap to make it ring. Three ornaments complete a little tree.

ideas.title: Their Song, Karaoke Edition
ideas.summary: An original song about them, presented as a karaoke screen with a glowing bouncing-ball lyric line, plus the render-it-yourself sheet so they can turn it into a full track.

ideas.title: The Mixtape of Your Year
ideas.summary: A cassette in a hand-labelled case. Put it in the deck, scrub the tape with your finger, flip to Side B. Each track is a short original tune named after a moment of their year, with liner notes.

ideas.title: The Music Box
ideas.summary: A wooden music box. Turn the crank and a melody composed for them plays while a tiny figure (their pet, them on skis) turns on top.

ideas.title: A Place You Can Hear
ideas.summary: A window onto a place they love — a mountain hut at night, their city in the rain. Sliders mix the sounds (wind, fire, rain, a dog snoring) to make their perfect background.

ideas.title: An Arcade Game Starring Them
ideas.summary: A small arcade game where they (or their pet) are the hero and their real nemeses are the enemies. Ends on a shareable high-score card.

ideas.title: The Crossword of Your Year
ideas.summary: A proper crossword where every clue is about their life, their people and their in-jokes. Solving it reveals a hidden message in the shaded squares.
ideas.suitable_if: You know at least 12 things about them.

ideas.title: The Bracket of Their Favourite Things
ideas.summary: A sports-style tournament bracket of 16 of their favourite things (foods, places, shows, habits). They pick winners round by round; the champion gets an absurdly grand trophy ceremony.
ideas.suitable_if: You know 16 favourites (or at least 8 for a smaller bracket).

ideas.title: The Puzzle Box
ideas.summary: A Japanese-style wooden puzzle box with hidden panels and a sequence they must find. Inside, something small and lovely.

ideas.title: The Idle Clicker of Their Life
ideas.summary: An absurd idle game where they produce the thing they produce most (commits, summits, cups of tea). Upgrades are real parts of their life, and the numbers get ridiculous.

ideas.title: The Award Ceremony
ideas.summary: A stage, a spotlight, an envelope. "And the award for Most Consistent Use of 'Quick Question' goes to…" Their name, a trophy, an applause button and an acceptance speech they can read aloud.

ideas.title: The Museum of One Object
ideas.summary: A grand museum exhibit dedicated to one mundane object they own (their water bottle, their old hiking boots), with a pedestal, a wall label, an audio guide, a "conservation history" and a gift shop.
ideas.suitable_if: You know an object they use a lot.

ideas.title: A Nature Documentary About Them
ideas.summary: A short animated wildlife documentary about their ordinary day, narrated with hushed reverence ("Here, in the glow of the second monitor, the builder prepares to deploy.").

ideas.title: The Annual Report of You
ideas.summary: A glossy corporate annual report about their life, with animated charts of absurd KPIs, a letter from the CEO (their pet), and a "risks and outlook" section.

ideas.title: An Official Patent for Their Habit
ideas.summary: A patent document, with technical drawings, for a habit or invention of theirs ("Method and apparatus for eating chocolate on a summit").

ideas.title: The Daily [Name]
ideas.summary: The front page of a newspaper entirely about them. Breaking news about trivial events, a weather report for their mood, classifieds from their pet.

ideas.title: Introducing Their Pet, The Product
ideas.summary: A slick product-launch page for their pet, with scroll animations, specs ("Shedding: industrial-grade"), colours, accessories and a "pre-order" button that does something silly.

ideas.title: Their 2027 Horoscope, Written by Their Pet
ideas.summary: A zodiac wheel where every sign is replaced by something from their life. Spin it to land on their month-by-month horoscope, written by their pet.
ideas.suitable_if: They have a pet, or swap the pet for a favourite fictional character's style.

ideas.title: The Trailer for Their Week
ideas.summary: An epic movie trailer for an ordinary week of theirs — title cards, a booming "In a world…" and a release date.

ideas.title: A Sticker Sheet Made for Them
ideas.summary: A die-cut sticker sheet in a style they'd love. Peel each sticker off and slap it onto the page (or their "laptop lid"). Includes print-ready files and real print services.

ideas.title: Wallpapers From Their World
ideas.summary: A generative art piece built from their themes. Click to regenerate until they find the one they like, then download it at their real phone and desktop sizes.

ideas.title: A Zine About Them
ideas.summary: An 8-page fold-and-staple zine about them, to read on screen (pages flip) or print on one sheet and fold. Includes a how-to-fold diagram.

ideas.title: The Constellation of Your Year
ideas.summary: A night sky. Each star is a moment from their year. Connect them in order and the lines draw a constellation in the shape of something they love.

ideas.title: The Time Capsule
ideas.summary: A letter from you about who they are this December, sealed in a capsule. It opens fully only on a date they choose next year. Until then, it shows how long is left.

ideas.title: A Hand-Drawn Map of Your Year
ideas.summary: An illustrated treasure-style map of the places in their year, with little notes, sea monsters for the bad weeks and an X for the best day.
ideas.suitable_if: You know places from their year.

ideas.title: Thank-You Letters From Their Things
ideas.summary: A small stack of envelopes from the objects in their life — their laptop, their boots, the coffee machine, the dog's lead — each thanking them in its own voice.

ideas.title: A Golden Ticket to Something Real
ideas.summary: A golden ticket that unfolds into a purchase-ready proposal for a real experience near them — a hut night, a class, a concert — with price, date checked, booking link and what's left for them to do.
ideas.suitable_if: Web research allowed and real-world suggestions are on.

ideas.title: A Book, Chosen for Them
ideas.summary: A library card and a bookplate with their name, for one book chosen for them, with a short reason, where to get it, and price checked.
ideas.suitable_if: Web research allowed and real-world suggestions are on.
